Disassembly: omni ivwb 2.55 u4.bin
=====================================

Source: same system as omni-ivwb-2.55-u3.bin (see that file and
        omni-ivwb-2.55.summary.md). This chip is a bank-switched code
        extension for U3 - see below (CONFIRMED, not hypothesized).

Architecture: Intel MCS-51 (8051-family) - decodes as plausible code
              throughout, but does NOT start with a standard interrupt
              vector table the way U3 does (expected - it's only ever
              entered via U3's bank-switch trampoline, never via reset).

Range disassembled: $0000-$F8FA (the used region - remainder is
                     unprogrammed $FF fill). Unlike U3, the two 32KB
                     halves of this image are NOT identical - the full
                     64KB is real content.

Method: linear-sweep disassembly, same tool/limitations as every other
        disassembly in this project.

CONFIRMED: U4 is a bank-switched code extension for U3, sharing the same
external (MOVX) memory map. U3 contains a call-out trampoline at
$4C5E-$4C83 that uses P1.0 as a bank-select line: it forces P1.0 low
then high (an edge, not just a level - suggesting an edge-latched bank
register), then jumps to a caller-supplied DPTR which now resolves
against U4's mapped content instead of U3's. U4 code returns via
"LJMP $4C7A", which restores P1.0's prior state and returns to the
original U3 caller. Seven fixed call sites were found in U3 - $0140,
$1B80, $1D44, $1D58, $3D4F, $4ECA, $647B - each loading a different
literal DPTR before calling the trampoline at $4C5E, i.e. seven
distinct, hardcoded entry points into U4's address space (not a generic
numbered-function table reachable from a menu number). See
omni-ivwb-2.55.protocol.md for the full trace, including the corrected
understanding of what one of these entry points ($984A) actually does
(a power-on default initializer for $4CE3-$4CE6, not a menu-driven save
as first suspected).

Other supporting evidence U4 shares U3's external memory map:
  - U4 references external memory address $4CE3 (twice) - the same
    address U3 reads for the hypothesized SPI device-address field
  - U4 has no embedded display-message text and no references to U3's
    message-table base ($6AE2) or response-buffer base ($882E) -
    consistent with U4 holding computational/control logic while U3
    owns the UI and serial protocol

Not attempted in this pass: full per-routine annotation of U4's content
beyond the seven known entry points, or finding whether any other,
not-yet-located entry points exist (e.g. reached from elsewhere in U3
that wasn't scanned for LCALL $4C5E specifically).
